title: test(rest): restore the #5821 ghost-path pin, whose input set had silently become empty (#6894)
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#6894

## Step 1 — re-measurement (the card's stop condition)

The card required re-measuring before implementing, and stopping if `stale` turned out to be non-empty today. It is empty. Measured on this branch through the **same `loadOpenApiSpec` seam the pin uses**, not by reading the file:

```
PROBE artifact top-level keys: openapi, info, servers, components, security
PROBE has own `paths` key: false
PROBE #5821 pin input set (stale paths): [] -> size 0
PROBE loop body executions: 0
PROBE cached object identity === returned: true
```

This reproduces #5969's recorded measurement exactly, so the card stands as an implementation rather than a wording-only fix. Confirmed at the producer too — `packages/spec/scripts/build-openapi.ts` on `origin/main` states it deliberately emits no route section, and the artifact has no `paths` key at all (absent, not empty).

## What changed

Only `packages/rest/src/rest-openapi-route.test.ts`. No production source touched.

The pin read the artifact's own `paths` and looped over them. That was the right input while spec still emitted a route section; #5744 removed the emission — correctly, ADR-0076, a section can only be produced by the package that mounts the routes — and the pin's input silently became the empty set.

The fix feeds the pin a constructed section rather than waiting for the producer to re-emit a removed defect, which would amount to requiring a production-side bug to keep a test alive:

- `staleArtifactPaths()` rebuilds the section the artifact carried until #5744, from the existing `PHANTOM_PATHS` list, including the historical `PUT` on a record so the fixture is the shape that really shipped.
- The discard case plants it on the object `loadOpenApiSpec` caches, then **reads the input back through the loader and requires it to be non-empty**. That assertion is the one that would have caught this bug: it turns "the loop found nothing to check" from a silent pass into a failure.
- The three surviving assertions (`components.schemas` key set, `securitySchemes` deep-equal, `info.title`) move into their own case, unchanged. They still bite and were never the problem.

## Bidirectional proof (the card's hard delivery criterion)

Prediction stated before running: the regression this pin exists to catch is the merge that #5588 ruling C forbids, so mutating `enriched.paths = builtin.paths` into `enriched.paths = { ...(spec.paths ?? {}), ...builtin.paths }` should turn **exactly one** case red — every other case serves the real path-less artifact, where a merge is a no-op.

**GREEN** (fixed test, unmutated production):

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  13 passed (13)
```

**RED** (fixed test, merge regression in `rest-server.ts`):

```
× ... > discards a `paths`-carrying artifact instead of merging it 22ms
  → stale artifact path '/api/{object}' leaked into the served document: expected { get: { …(2) } } to be undefined
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 12 passed (13)
```

One red, on the intended case, as predicted.

**CONTROL — the same regression against the OLD test file** (`git checkout origin/main -- packages/rest/src/rest-openapi-route.test.ts`, mutation still in place):

```
✓ ... > discards the static artifact section even though spec still emits it 5ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  12 passed (12)
```

This is the measurement that matters most. Under an identical, real leak the old pin reports green — direct evidence that the layer was dead, not merely narrow. The new pin catches what the old one could not.

**GREEN again** after reverting the mutation: 13 passed. The mutation was transient and never committed; `git diff origin/main -- packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` is empty and the PR diff is one file.

Note on the file-surface boundary declared in the claim: the fix needed no production edit and made none. The production mutation above exists only as the reverse-verification's temporary experiment, applied and reverted inside this isolated worktree, and is not part of the diff.

## Wording that had expired

- Case title `discards the static artifact section even though spec still emits it` — spec no longer emits it.
- Comment `Leg 2 (#5744) removes the spec-side generation. Until it lands, ...` — it landed.

Both are rewritten to today's state, with the re-measurement recorded in the fixture's doc comment so the next reader sees why the input is a fixture.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest test` — 73 files / 1143 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest typecheck` — clean. Note this package's `tsconfig.json` excludes `*.test.ts`, so that run does not cover the edited file; measured separately with tests included, branch vs `origin/main` under identical conditions: **152 total errors both sides, the same 2 pre-existing TS2835 in this file both sides — delta 0**, so the `@objectstack/rest` `TEST_DEBT: 163` ratchet cannot move.
- All 34 gate steps in the ESLint job of `.github/workflows/lint.yml`, run one by one: all PASS (includes `check:nul-bytes`, `check:route-envelope`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:engine-double-contract`).
- Type-check job gates: 19 PASS. Four (`check:type-check-debt`, `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage`, `check:app-nav-i18n`) refused to run without a full workspace build, each self-reporting "Nothing was checked/measured"; CI builds first. The debt one is covered by the delta measurement above.
- `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs` plus a control-byte self-scan of the edited file: clean.

## Changeset

Deliberately none. Test-only, no user-visible effect, nothing released — this takes the `skip-changeset` route.
